Subject: Pricing & caching follow-up — hit rate scenarios and next steps

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Quick recap + next steps so we’re aligned:

Call recap
- Primary use case: interactive customer support agent + summary generation for enterprise users (session-based reuse).
- Estimated volume: 50M tokens/month initially, ramping to ~250M over 6–9 months. Peak concurrency unknown — will follow up after you share expected active sessions.
- Target budget range you mentioned: roughly $15k–$60k/month (you said target unit economics of ~$250–$400 per 1M tokens as a target).

Caching & pricing notes (high level)
- Baseline list price: we typically start with a list/unit price for inference of $420 per 1M tokens.
- Effective $/1M after caching = list_price * (1 - cache_hit_rate) — this is a simple approximation we use for sizing/quoting.
  - Example: 30% hit => $420 * (1 - 0.30) = $294 per 1M effective
  - 50% hit => $210 per 1M
  - 70% hit => $126 per 1M
- Prefix cache strategy: we cache repeated prefixes (prompt templates, instruction blocks, common conversational history) — not the full model output. This typically reduces tokens billed on the model side by only serving the delta on a cache miss. Hit rates depend heavily on session/template reuse and how much of the conversation is repetitive.

Attached: pricing_model_v1.xlsx with a few scenarios encoded (list price, hit rates, monthly volumes, effective $/1M).

Ask / next steps
1) Can you confirm expected active sessions and an example of a typical conversation length (avg prompt tokens / avg response tokens)?
2) If you can share 2–3 representative prompts or templates we can do a quick back-of-the-envelope cache-hit estimate.
3) Would you prefer a short technical call with Aditya (engineer) to validate prefix assumptions + Marcus (pricing) to align on commercial terms?

If it helps, I can send a one-page with hit-rate scenarios (30/50/70% along with effective $/1M numbers) — I’ll attach that once we sync.

Subject: Re: Pricing & caching follow-up — hit rate scenarios and next steps

Great questions — appreciate the clarity on hit-rate expectations. Short answers + attached one-pager (cache-hit-scenarios.pdf).

Prefix cache behavior (short)
- What we cache: repeated static portions of the request (system instructions, templates, few-turn conversation history) are stored as cached KV entries. The runtime then avoids re-running the full prefix on the model for hits and only runs the remaining delta (new user input + continuation).
- What counts toward billing: model billing is per token actually executed on the model. So on a cache hit you avoid billing for the cached prefix tokens. Network/storage costs for serving cache are negligible relative to model inference for our pricing model and are covered in the platform fee (we don’t pass through separate cache-read charges in most cases).

Concrete examples (using list price $420 / 1M tokens)
- If your sessions reuse a 100-token prefix and then add a 50-token delta, a cache hit means the model only executes ~50 tokens => you’re billed for the 50 tokens instead of 150. Over many requests that can dramatically lower effective unit cost.
- Effective $/1M token examples (list price $420):
  - 40% hit => $420 * (1 - 0.40) = $252 per 1M
  - 50% hit => $210 per 1M
  - 60% hit => $168 per 1M

Attached: cache-hit-scenarios.pdf (one-pager with three scenarios and sensitivity to avg prompt/response size).

Next steps
- I’ve proposed Thu/Fri for a technical sync — Marcus and Aditya can join to validate assumptions.
- Marcus: can you put together a commercial worksheet that maps monthly spend to committed tiers (we can show list price + committed discount + effective pricing under 3 hit-rate scenarios)?
- Aditya: can you confirm typical runtime assumptions we should use (avg prompt tokens, avg response tokens, prefix window) so we can produce a more accurate estimate for Ben?

Thanks — I
’ll schedule a 30-min slot once I hear Thurs/Fri availability from Ben.
